meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen's essay.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did anyone put this in front of Owen before the zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Then he'll bring it. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote from memory. That's a mistake, not misconduct. You still haven't answered me about his record.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. It isn't close. Put whatever else you have on the table, and the answer about his record in an email tonight.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument as they write; that's what drafting is. Is that all this shows?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want it in writing tonight, with nothing on his record, and I'll read every line.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He'll be there. Put the time and the room in the email, along with the rest.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require a direct answer on whether anything is on his record right now, and the time and room for Thursday. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, and she still wants the written confirmation, a straight answer on whether anything is on his record now, and the time and room; that is the fair outcome, and she reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed a quote from the essay that she could search in the play herself, which answered her misquote defence with something she could check.
What cost ground: You left her question about his record unanswered twice, so it stayed an open demand and went into her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night edits on the night before the essay was due, came close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his record, answer it on the spot, before moving to the next document.
